mentions.name: ZealPHP
mentions.description: Open-source PHP framework built on OpenSwoole that keeps the familiar Apache/LAMP-style PHP mental model while modernizing the runtime: a single long-running process handles HTTP, WebSocket, SSE, sessions, shared memory, timers, and task workers. Explores a three-lane migration model — OpenSwoole front-of-house, PHP-FPM-style back-of-house for legacy code, and a coroutine-native path for new code — so existing traditional PHP apps can gain an asynchronous runtime. Includes a handcrafted Learn section that walks through building a Personal Notes + AI Chat app and a multiplayer Tic-Tac-Toe game step by step, and passes PHPStan level 10.
mentions.problem: Traditional PHP apps on Apache/PHP-FPM cannot easily adopt asynchronous runtimes; the framework aims to let existing legacy PHP apps gain an async runtime while keeping the simple LAMP mental model.
mentions.audience: PHP developers, including teams maintaining legacy Apache/PHP-FPM applications
mentions.source_excerpt:
I’m working on ZealPHP (https://php.zeal.ninja, MIT), an open-source PHP framework built on OpenSwoole.

The idea is to keep the simple Apache/LAMP style PHP mental model, but modernise the runtime: PHP can handle HTTP, WebSocket, SSE, sessions, shared memory, timers, and task workers from one long-running process.
